newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee firms on rising call money rates.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee firms on rising call money rates.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee rose against the dollar in Tuesday morning trade as banks scrambled for rupees on rising call money rates, dealers said.
At 0430 GMT, the rupee was at 56.60 to the dollar after opening at 56.65. On Monday, it closed at 56.64 after rising to 56.53 during the day, dealers said.
Overnight call money opened at 30 percent and dropped slightly to 26 percent, but quickly recovered to 30 percent.
"Money rates are high. The holding cost of dollars is high. Because of that, the rupee is rising," a Deutsche Bank dealer said.
Call money rates are believed to be high since the central bank took 1.1 billion rupees out of the system at last week's Treasury Bill auctions, a Commercial Bank dealer said.
The central bank, responding to the dollar's strengthening overseas, pushed the greenback up by 3.25 local cents and fixed buying and selling rates at 55.9523 and 57.0827, respectively.

"We don't expect the market to be very active today," the Deutsche Bank dealer said. "Most banks are short of rupees and everybody wants to sell dollars. It's not the ideal situation for active trading."
